records.name: Aurora Flight Sciences
records.overview:
Aurora's Manassas airport campus combines engineering and build spaces, test laboratories, three hangars and remote flight-operations centers. Its flight-operations offering includes system integration, test crews, hardware-in-the-loop simulation and operator training. These resources can help a developer evaluate a sensor, autonomous behavior or operating procedure in simulation before a coordinated flight campaign. Aurora's aircraft and mobile operations resources are a company-wide offering, not a promise that every aircraft or test takes place in Manassas.

Bring the payload interfaces, intended behavior, data requirements and proposed operating conditions to the flight-operations team. Agree the test location, aircraft configuration, safety and authorization responsibilities, crew support, deliverables and commercial scope. Mississippi and West Virginia composite-manufacturing equipment should not be attributed to this Virginia campus, and published hangars are not an open-access range reservation.
records.partnership_opportunities: Contact Aurora about engineering programs and aircraft-development partnerships. Facility visits and use of test resources require company arrangements.
records.short_description: Manassas aircraft-development campus with hangars, engineering build spaces, test laboratories, and remote flight-operations centers.

records.name: Austal USA Advanced Technologies and Solutions
records.overview:
Austal USA's Charlottesville Solutions division develops and integrates autonomous-maritime platforms and mission technologies. Its published scope includes unmanned surface vessels, modular payload architectures, machinery health monitoring and lifecycle support; underwater vehicles are described as a growth area rather than an established local product line. These capabilities can support a discussion about vessel autonomy, mission-system interfaces or sustainment data.

A customer or technology partner should identify the platform, payload, integration boundaries, reliability needs and proposed program, then request the appropriate Solutions team through Austal's inquiry form. Confirm current engineering scope, production site, demonstrations, eligibility and contractual arrangements. The Charlottesville office is not the company's Mobile shipyard, and its listing does not establish a Virginia waterfront test site, local vessel-construction capacity or permission to conduct autonomous operations.

records.name: AutoBoat at Virginia Tech
records.overview:
AutoBoat is a student-led Ware Lab team that designs and builds autonomous sailboats and high-power electric motorboats. The team's published work includes hulls, electronics and software for the International Robotic Sailing Regatta and Promoting Electric Propulsion competitions. This provides hands-on experience in navigation, marine structures, propulsion integration and autonomy through complete student prototypes, rather than a commercial fleet or a public maritime test range.

The team invites sponsorship and partnerships through autoboat@vt.edu and recruits students into software, electronics, mechanical and business subteams. A potential partner can discuss a defined component, mentoring, data or sponsorship contribution and agree expectations with the team. Confirm the current project, staff/student availability, intellectual property, safety and actual water-testing arrangements; the campus reference point is not a boat-launch permission or a guaranteed external testing service.
records.short_description: Student engineering team designing fully autonomous robotic sailboats and electric motorboats.

records.name: Autonomous Aerial Vehicles at Virginia Tech
records.overview:
AAV is a student-run engineering design team that develops autonomous aircraft for payload delivery, obstacle avoidance, mapping and search-and-rescue tasks. Its published organization includes software, structures and administration subteams, with competition participation in RoboNation SUAS and C-UASC. A partner can connect with students working across aircraft hardware, perception, navigation and mission integration rather than treating the entry as a standalone commercial testing center.

Use the team's published email to discuss sponsorship, mentoring, a component contribution or a bounded student project. Identify the intended mission, interfaces, data and educational goals and confirm the current academic-year plan and faculty/laboratory involvement. Aircraft availability, flight sites, approvals, insurance, supervision and deliverables need separate arrangements. A competition result or campus marker is not a general flight authorization or a promise of contract-development capacity.
records.short_description: Student engineering team developing autonomous aircraft for payload delivery, obstacle avoidance, mapping, and search and rescue.

A potential collaborator can approach Abhishek Phadke with the aircraft, software, sensing, trajectory or teaching objective and the measurements required. The description of high ceilings and larger drones is not a published weight/span limit or a public booking policy. Classroom exam preparation also does not itself confer a pilot certificate or outdoor flight authorization.
records.partnership_opportunities: The lab is intended to support researchers and industry partners; program questions can be directed to Professor Abhishek Phadke.

records.name: CNU Capable Humanitarian Robotics and Intelligent Systems Lab
records.overview:
CNU's CHRISLab studies high-level robot behavior intended to reduce human exposure to hazardous environments and support assistive applications. Its current research description identifies open-source ROS 2 tools, including FlexBE hierarchical state machines, and work toward verifiable synthesis of behaviors from user-defined tasks. This is useful for discussing how an operator specifies, supervises or adapts a robot mission, rather than simply requesting a generic autonomy demonstration.

The university names David Conner and robotics@cnu.edu as research contacts. Bring the robot/software stack, task definition, failure conditions and validation question to the team and agree a collaboration scope, deliverables and intellectual-property terms. Confirm hardware, supervision and access directly. Correct-by-construction behavior synthesis is a research objective, not a blanket certification that a resulting robot is safe for an unrestricted operational deployment.
records.short_description: CNU lab developing verifiable autonomous robotic behaviors for human-support applications.

records.name: Fairlead Maritime Systems
records.overview:
Fairlead offers maritime control-system engineering, power and energy-system integration, build-to-print manufacturing, modular structures, and vessel sustainment across several Hampton Roads facilities. Its integration services cover system architecture, testing, and validation, which can be relevant when a maritime autonomy developer needs the supporting electrical, control, or fabricated systems around a platform.

Start with the system interfaces, operating environment, applicable requirements, production quantity, and acceptance plan, then ask Fairlead to identify the appropriate technical team and location. Corporate waterfront acreage and pier frontage describe a combined industrial footprint, not the headquarters parcel or space available to a particular customer. Arrange any site visit and confirm equipment, project eligibility, schedule, and commercial terms directly.
records.partnership_opportunities: Request a capability discussion for maritime controls, power integration, build-to-print components, modular structures, or sustainment. Confirm the work location rather than assuming all services occur at headquarters.
records.short_description: Portsmouth shipbuilder and systems integrator with active unmanned-platform work and a 2026 partnership to scale AEGIR unmanned surface vessel production.

Confirm material acceptance, machine envelope, certification scope, and current capacity before selecting a supplier.

records.overview:

Its published work covers airport and airspace modeling, rare-event risk, flight-deck human factors, noise/emissions and cost-benefit analysis, with resources on drones and autonomy. This is a connection for evaluating an operating concept or airspace/system tradeoff, not a physical test range that can authorize an aircraft to fly.

A sponsor can approach Lance Sherry with the proposed service or aircraft concept, routes and demand assumptions, operational constraints, available data and decision criteria. Define the model, scenarios, validation evidence, uncertainty and deliverables with the research team. Confirm the current project, staff, software/data rights and collaboration arrangements directly; historical studies and a university office do not establish regulator approval, current operating permission or open-access flight facilities.

records.name: George Mason RobotiXX Laboratory
records.overview:

Its published platforms include off-road wheeled vehicles, Jackal and Husky robots, mobile manipulators and legged robots. Examples include navigation through constrained obstacles, mobility over uneven terrain, passive night perception and human-aware navigation. Public benchmarks, datasets and robot-platform descriptions provide concrete starting points for evaluating an autonomy method.

A developer or research sponsor can discuss a navigation failure mode, sensing configuration, terrain scenario, benchmark or field-evaluation collaboration with director Xuesu Xiao. Agree which hardware, data, metrics and site would be used, plus safety, project funding and intellectual-property terms. Listed robots are research assets, not a rental inventory; manufacturer performance figures do not define a universal test-site envelope or public access to field locations.
records.short_description: Field-robotics laboratory developing motion-planning and machine-learning methods for robust mobile autonomy.

records.name: Linebird
records.overview:
Linebird's Osprey Nonconductive Payload System lets compatible drones carry sensors and tools for contact work on electric infrastructure. Its published aerial-ohmmeter application assesses splice and dead-end connector health on transmission lines, extending inspection beyond imagery alone. The Richmond company also discusses restoration, wildlife mitigation and supply-transport concepts; these should be evaluated as specific product applications rather than assumed services available with every aircraft.

Use the published company contact or demonstration request to discuss the inspection problem, aircraft/payload compatibility, measurements and reporting needed. Confirm the exact configuration, training, operating procedures, utility permissions, electrical safety responsibilities and commercial support before considering energized-line work. A product demonstration or nonconductive payload does not independently authorize a flight or qualify a crew for live-line operations, and the Richmond address is not a public test range.

records.name: Newport News Park Radio Control Club Flying Field
records.overview:
NNPRCC publishes a 400-foot paved runway, a 30-acre overfly area, DC charging power, shelters and spectator facilities for model-aircraft activity. The field is open to members from sunrise to sunset, and the club welcomes visitors and guests to meet members. It supports model-aircraft building, pilot practice and supervised community learning; those amenities do not make it an unrestricted commercial UAS test range.

Contact nnprcc@gmail.com about membership, guest arrangements, training and the current field rules before flying. Members must follow club and Academy of Model Aeronautics requirements. The club states a 400-foot height restriction because of the nearby airport, but users must still resolve all applicable aircraft and airspace requirements. The existing field and a future Mobility Innovation Center activity have separate access and approval arrangements; runway length is not a certified aircraft acceptance limit.

This shipyard should not be presented as a general USV factory or an unrestricted marine test basin.

The Small Business Office provides assistance and advocacy; registration or an inquiry does not establish a contract award. Visits require coordination with an NNS representative and compliance with site security and safety instructions, including the applicable industrial protective equipment. Define the actual shipbuilding work package before seeking access or sharing controlled technical material.

NOVA's Trailside Building Fab Lab supports digital fabrication, 3D modeling, electronics/coding, robotics and additive manufacturing. It can help students prototype an enclosure, bracket, sensor interface or simple robotic mechanism and develop practical fabrication skills. Published programs include workshops, class collaborations, design challenges and open-lab personal projects; this is education and prototyping capacity rather than an established outside contract-manufacturing service.

The NOVA Makers open-lab route is for NOVA students, faculty and staff. The college requires enrollment in its Canvas course, completion of the online safety-orientation certification and a release form before open-lab participation; individual equipment and workshops can require further certifications. Contact the Fab Lab to discuss eligibility, a tour, class partnership, materials, equipment and current hours. Do not assume commercial access, unsupervised machine use or that a robotics-capable makerspace permits drone flights.

records.name: NSWC Dahlgren Outdoor Autonomy Laboratory
records.overview:
Dahlgren's Outdoor Autonomy Lab supports early prototypes and low-risk checkouts with ground, surface and underwater robots and radio-frequency systems. The Navy's August 2024 account identifies open/wooded terrain and a pond, intended to bridge bench development and larger evaluations. A planned operations-center conversion was still future-facing in that account; it is not presented here as completed. The published scope does not establish a general aerial-drone range.

The Navy states that government personnel can lead projects after lab training and that contractors, universities and industry require government sponsorship. Bring a defined test objective, vehicle, risk assessment, measurements and support needs to the sponsoring team. Confirm current rules, configurations, approvals, site access and availability. The Small Business Office can route engagement questions but cannot grant range access, and the locality marker does not identify the lab entrance or operating boundary.

records.name: Polaris Semiconductor
records.overview:
Polaris Semiconductor develops low-noise power regulators using photovoltaic-output optocouplers to reduce the switching noise associated with conventional converters. Its published families include buck, boost and ultra-low-noise devices, with evaluation boards, datasheets and SPICE models offered for design work. For an autonomy hardware team, the relevant use is clean power for RF, precision sensors or imaging electronics, subject to application-specific qualification. This Alexandria company is not evidence of a Virginia wafer foundry.

The engineering contact form supports sample/quote requests, design-in support and partnerships and asks for product interest and input/output voltages. Discuss noise bandwidth, current, thermal conditions, package, reliability and validation evidence before selecting a part. The company distinguishes radiation-tolerance testing from complete-package radiation-hardness-assurance qualification, which remains on its roadmap. Confirm the exact device, available test reports, procurement terms and manufacturing traceability directly.
records.short_description: Power-management semiconductor developer offering low-noise voltage regulators for aerospace, defense and precision instrumentation.

records.name: UVA Bio-Inspired Engineering Research Laboratory
records.overview:
UVA's Bio-Inspired Engineering Research Laboratory investigates structures and actuation inspired by biological movement. Founder Hilary Bart-Smith's university profile describes manta-ray-like morphing foils, lightweight lattice structures, electro-active polymers and applications to morphing aircraft wings and micro air vehicles. These capabilities are relevant to early-stage studies of underwater propulsion, adaptable structures and unconventional robotic mechanisms, not off-the-shelf AUV sales.

A collaborator can discuss a proposed fin or wing mechanism, material behavior, actuation concept, structural model or experimental validation question. Approach the faculty team with geometry, load and motion requirements, intended measurements and a proposed research scope. Confirm current equipment, project support, intellectual-property arrangements and laboratory access; no public tank-rental service, vehicle acceptance envelope or unrestricted field-testing permission is established by the faculty description.
records.short_description: Research laboratory developing bio-inspired structures, controls, and aquatic robotic concepts.

records.name: UVA Coastal Research Center UAS Operations
records.overview:
UVA's Coastal Research Center provides a coastal fieldwork base and access coordination for Eastern Shore research. Its operator policy requires drone-pilot compliance documents before drone-based work from centre property or vessels. Research on nearby islands and shorelines also depends on the relevant land manager's access, collection, and deployment permissions, with seasonal wildlife restrictions in some areas.

The resource can support a proposed coastal mapping, habitat-monitoring, or other drone-based research campaign when the centre agrees the project. Discuss the location, aircraft, payload, takeoff/recovery arrangements, vessel needs, people and data plan with staff. Campus acreage is not an authorized flight boundary, and permission to use a centre boat or property does not establish unrestricted access to the surrounding protected lands.
records.short_description: Coastal research-center UAS operations for compliant flights from the center's property and vessels.

records.name: VIMS Autonomous Systems Laboratory
records.overview:
The VIMS Autonomous Systems Laboratory designs and builds free-swimming robots for oceanographic research. Mark Patterson's published research profile describes AUV sampling of the seabed and water column, sonar-based recognition of fish and krill, and measurements associated with oxygen conditions and coral-reef health. These examples connect vehicle autonomy to a defined scientific measurement problem rather than simply listing generic marine-robotics capabilities.

A research partner can discuss a sensing question, sampling strategy, recognition algorithm or vehicle behavior with the laboratory's published faculty contact. Identify the sensors, environmental conditions, survey scale and data products needed. Confirm which platforms and personnel are currently available, project sponsorship, deployment arrangements and applicable permissions. Research objectives such as long-duration swarms should not be treated as a commercially available vehicle specification or guaranteed endurance.

Published glider work describes temperature/salinity, oxygen, fluorescence and optical-backscatter sensing, providing examples of how autonomous sampling can characterize water masses and ecosystem conditions. The glider page contains historical missions; it is not a current inventory or a promise that the described vehicles are available for hire.

A partner can approach lab director Donglai Gong with a survey area, scientific question, desired depth and sampling resolution, sensor requirements and data-delivery needs. Discuss platform selection, integration, deployment/recovery support, project funding and permissions before planning fieldwork. The Gloucester Point research contact is distinct from an approved deployment location or a general-purpose maritime test range.

records.name: Virginia Tech SpaceDrones Laboratory
records.overview:
SpaceDrones uses hardware and software testbeds, spacecraft simulation and surrogate aerial platforms to study autonomous space applications. Virginia Tech's ICAT profile describes hardware-in-the-loop work using multirotor drones, camera/LiDAR sensing and projected optical scenes to simulate aspects of free-flying spacecraft. It also documents multi-agent coordination experiments using lighter-than-air vehicles as surrogates for harder-to-deploy systems. These are laboratory simulations, not orbital qualification or a substitute for vacuum, thermal or launch testing.

A collaborator can ask Kevin Schroeder about relative-navigation, perception, cooperative-control or proximity-operations experiments. Define the scene, sensors, dynamics to be represented, algorithm and ground-truth measurements, then confirm current configuration, space, vehicle acceptance, project terms and safety procedures. The ICAT examples include dated 2022-24 projects and do not guarantee that every demonstrated configuration is presently available.
records.short_description: Collaborative hardware and software laboratory for autonomous space applications, distributed UAS, and vision-based tracking.

records.name: Virginia Tech Stability Wind Tunnel
records.overview:
Virginia Tech's Stability Wind Tunnel provides aerodynamic and aeroacoustic experiments for academic and industrial projects. Published specifications include a 1.85-by-1.85-m test section, speeds up to 80 m/s, and a removable anechoic test section. These are tunnel specifications, not a maximum aircraft span or flight envelope.

Airfoil, rotor-noise, and computational-validation work can help refine an air-vehicle design before outdoor testing. Contact the tunnel team with the model geometry, mounting and load requirements, desired speeds, instrumentation, and acoustic measurements. The university publishes a major-upgrade plan, so confirm the available configuration and schedule. This laboratory is not an open-air UAS range.

records.name: Virginia Tech Transportation Institute

Its Smart Roads combine highway, reconfigurable surface-street, rural and unimproved environments with controllable lighting, weather-making, sensors and communications. The institute also describes garages, machine/electronics shops and instrumented vehicles for developing and collecting test data. These are distinct resources, not one universally available equipment package.

An ADS or sensor developer can discuss repeatable scenarios, degraded-weather evaluation, vehicle instrumentation, driver interaction or simulation-to-road validation. Define the vehicle, scenario, measures, data rights and required physical support before requesting a project. Coordinate any transition to public roads or aerial testing separately, with the relevant approvals; the institute's published capabilities are not permission for an unrelated vehicle or drone to operate there.

records.overview:
WR Systems' Norfolk operations centre supports engineering and integration for uncrewed surface vessels. Its published unmanned-systems scope includes autonomous navigation, vessel control, sensors, communications, payload integration, cybersecurity support, and test planning through factory-acceptance and underway testing. WR also describes support for the Unmanned Maritime Autonomy Architecture.

A vessel builder or operator can discuss integrating navigation, control and mission equipment into an existing platform, or supporting it through its lifecycle. Bring the vessel/interface baseline, payload requirements, desired autonomy functions and acceptance tests. The Norfolk office is distinct from Fairfax headquarters; confirm where fabrication, shore testing and on-water activities would occur for the actual contract.
